claim: \emph{Two protections in DocAble's job-recovery protocol.} A durable compare-and-set prevents competing workers from acquiring the same claim for a protected effect. A bounded explicit-state checker examines recovery interleavings, including whether a stale release can clear a newer worker's claim. The runtime constraint directly restricts execution; the checker evaluates the modeled protocol. Tests provide separate evidence about the implementation.

alt: DocAble job-recovery protocol with two obligations and two protections. At left, only one worker may acquire an effect claim; atomic compare-and-set restricts acquisition to the required stored state. At right, a stale release must not clear a newer claim; an explicit-state checker explores bounded interleavings. The lower boxes distinguish runtime constraint from model analysis.
